newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE wheat nervous, up on worldwide weather fears.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE wheat nervous, up on worldwide weather fears.

text.p: LIFFE grain ended higher, but off the day's highs, after a day of weather inspired rises, traders said.

On wheat, the emphasis was on the new crop, with November most active. It last traded 1.25 stg higher at 101.40 stg, well off a day's high of 102.00 stg, on volume of 262 lots. Total wheat volume was 759 lots.

The cause of the rises was a combination of continued weather concerns in Europe, along with the effects of sharp rises at the CBOT, where wheat opened up the 20 cent per bushel limit on Monday after weekend temperatures in the U.S. plains fell to record lows, one trader said.
"It's wrong to argue that the CBOT pushed London up, but it is an influence," one trader said. "The crucial thing is now whether the CBOT takes up extended limits on Tuesday," he said.

A rising CBOT and, hence, world prices, would leave room for European grains to get more expensive. But some were speculating that it could enable the EU to re-introduce a tax, rather than a refund on export licences, in a bid to prevent European prices rising too far, the trader said.

The market's nervousness explained how it ended off highs, he said. "It's a weather market. You're bound to get some profit taking," he said. Much of that profit taking was by market players trying to protect themselves, just in case an unexpected change in the weather triggers a sharp sell off.

No rain is forecast in Britain this week, with the exception of some showers in the far north-east, the meteorological office said. There is no rain forecast, either, in the major producing areas of the continent.
Just 11 lots of barley were traded, one on September, five on November and five on January. November last traded 1.25 stg higher at 98.25 stg.
